timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: They wanted to put me on a horse for the handover. Nigga, I just won fifty-two cars. Lord Orlan stood beside the white horse outside the palace gate, holding a ceremonial schedule. The horse ate a leaf off the hedge. Tradition, Orlan said. Does tradition have a transmission? Tank bent over laughing. Orlan checked his schedule as though it might contain an answer about gears.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna stroked the horse's neck. It leaned toward her hand immediately. Shameless nigga. Hadn't even introduced himself. I like him, she said. I looked at her. Looked at the horse. Welcome to the family, nigga. Orlan offered me the reins. I accepted them. The horse promptly took another leaf. We leaving? I asked. He's eating, Shawna said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, so was I when all this tradition arrived. The groom helped position him. I mounted. A cheer went up from people who had watched me drive through considerably worse arrangements, and the horse turned his head at the noise. Yeah, I told him. Get used to that. Shawna settled into the open carriage beside me. Tank and the others followed in the carriage behind.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: We started down toward the harbor at a speed that gave every balcony time to offer an opinion. Workers waved from doorways. Musicians raised their instruments. Women from Blue Hour shook blue scarves overhead. Drivers who had spent a month trying to pass me stood shouting my name while a horse did a perfectly ordinary walk. Sit kinglier! Tank called. Nigga, I'm sitting. But kinglier.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I straightened. The horse stopped to inspect something in the road. The whole procession stopped with him. Shawna covered her mouth. Don't, I told her. I haven't said anything. Your shoulders saying plenty. The groom clicked his tongue. The horse moved on. Behind us Tank started cheering again, completely out of proportion to the accomplishment.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, I won seven keys and fifty-two cars, and this hairy bastard had everybody impressed because he resumed walking. The shipyard was open. All the remaining workers on Luc's list had been found alive, along with others whose names hadn't reached us. Some had already left the island. Some stayed to collect wages from the seized race funds.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Some simply sat in the sun with food and a phone, doing nothing a rich man could turn into an obligation. Lark and Mateo went there together before the ceremony. They came back with grease on their hands and a list of people who wanted work at their new garage. Good mechanics? I asked. Better than good, Lark said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, hire them before somebody gets intelligent. Mercedes and Porsche had taken over the former guesthouse at the eastern quay for No Second Door. The first thing they removed was the little side entrance marked STAFF ONLY. They didn't tear out the wall. They changed where people were greeted and made the main doors wide enough for everybody's pride. Alina would help run it.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Rocco invested after Porsche made him say the number without smiling like he expected applause for paying a fair share. Nero and Cassius claimed the old racing shed. Esteban brought his tools. Inez brought three cars and an opinion about every shelf. Within an hour, the place sounded so alive with argument that I could hear it from the road.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, some buildings need a family fighting over where the wrench goes before they become home. At the harbor, the Sovereign Sun waited beneath a forest of flags. Celadon stood on the bridge in his old captain's coat. Renee stood beside him, one hand on his arm. The crew lined the decks, clean uniforms, shoulders straight. The white bird flew above them all.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: On the quay, Marcellus had arranged the seven keys in order inside their case. The real Blue Mercy shone on his hand as he touched the last one, checking it like a father straightening a son's tie before a wedding. You good? I asked him. The key is. Nigga, I meant you. He looked up at the ship. Then at the island behind us.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Yes, he said. I believe I am. Odette joined us before the ceremony. She spoke quietly enough that the crowd couldn't turn the news into entertainment. Morcant's body was recovered this morning. His death is confirmed. Bellario remains in custody on the mainland. He has given names, payments and the locations of the duke's remaining accounts. I nodded. The workers?

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Everyone on the list is accounted for. That was the part I had needed. She held out her hand. Captain. I shook it. Commandant. You are welcome in my harbor. Nigga, even with the car? Her mouth twitched. Please arrive by one method at a time. I couldn't promise that, so I kissed her hand instead and let her laugh at the evasion.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: A boyish-looking reporter in a very adult suit asked whether he could interview the horse. He was twenty-seven and, apparently, had spent the month watching me until ordinary journalism left his body. "Nigga, ask the horse," I said. "He won't answer." "Then that nigga got better press discipline than me." Tank leaned toward the microphone.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Horse says Aiden heavy with greatness." "Nigga," Shawna said, "leave the horse out of your mouth." The reporter laughed and turned the camera toward her instead. "Wise nigga," I said. "Always interview the wife when the men start translating livestock." The handover began at noon. Orlan read the old race proclamation from a book bound in blue leather.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The winner of the Grand Prix of Kings would receive the prize fleet and Isla Gloria, including the palace, the harbor estates and the race properties, witnessed by the flagship's captain and the assembled competitors. Aurelio had spent years making the words sound grand without letting them become true. Nigga, I stood there with all seven keys. Words were having an excellent day.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Celadon rang the ship's bell. I put the seventh key into the old harbor lock. It turned smoothly. Marcellus made a small satisfied sound beside me. Across the water, Celadon turned the second lock on the flagship's bridge. The ceremonial chain lowered at the harbor mouth, and the Sovereign Sun moved forward through the opened entrance while horns sounded from every boat in the bay.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Forty road cars waited along the quay. Twelve racing cars stood beneath the palace banners. Six yachts answered the flagship's bell. Isla Gloria opened around us like a hand. Lord Orlan knelt. Nigga, I had not asked him to do that. The crowd loved it so much he stayed down long enough to make sure the photographers had found his better side.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He held up the island deed. To Aiden, he said. Winner of every stage. Captain of the Grand Prix. Lord of Isla Gloria. Tank made a sound from somewhere behind me that I can only describe as a man trying to become a stadium. The crowd answered. Aiden. Aiden. Aiden. I took the deed. Then I took Shawna's hand and pulled her beside me.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, I told the crowd, I told y'all she wanted the ocean. Shawna covered her face, laughing. The harbor shook with applause. We walked the fleet afterward. A blue Ferrari for Shawna. A white Bentley because she liked the back seat. A silver roadster for Rosa, who looked at Tank and said, You can drive if you stop fighting the turns.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: A gold coupe for Mercedes. A black convertible for Porsche, who accepted it graciously and immediately asked where the second key was. Cassius chose a racing car for the restored family team. Inez chose one faster than his and smiled when he noticed. Nero took no new car.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He stood beside the White Heron with one hand on its roof and said he already had the one he wanted. Bruno tried to get into three cars before finding one that respected the width of his shoulders. When he finally sat down comfortably, he looked up at me with the gratitude of a man who had spent his whole adult life apologizing to upholstery.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, this is a real seat. Drive it strong. I'll drive it seated. Tank wanted the biggest coupe in the fleet. I gave it to him, and he grinned like I had handed him a new argument against doors. But his original black Mercedes was still safe in Vegas, shipped home before the Monaco month with the things we didn't need on the road.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: He said he wanted it waiting when we landed. Nigga, that car know me, he said. This one can learn. Yeah. But the Mercedes knows Rosa's side. I looked at him. He looked away. Nigga, don't make it poetry. Too late. The afternoon became a party large enough to need directions. Food in the square. Music on the quay. Champagne on the yachts.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Cards in the palace garden. Beautiful adults carrying on in rooms that had previously been reserved for men who confused money with permission to be dull. Mercedes and Porsche's friends filled the balconies with color, laughter and the kind of frank flirting that made rich men suddenly remember how to ask a question politely.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I was offered drinks, cigars, business partnerships, jewelry and three separate declarations that somebody had never seen a man move through the world like me. Nigga, I told the third man, you should see me shop for groceries. He said he had. Clementine's owner had sent him the video. At sunset, we went to the opera house. The bullet marks were still outside.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The damaged wall had been covered for the evening, not erased. Inside, every seat was full. Workers in borrowed jackets sat beside old aristocrats. Drivers leaned from the balconies. The musicians who had been dismissed stood in the pit again, looking at one another with a nervous happiness that made Valentina clear her throat twice before raising the baton. I sat in the front row.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tank and Rosa had argued over whether he should sit close enough to distract her. Rosa won. He sat beside me, which meant the first row now contained more devoted attention than the stage lights. Shawna came out in blue. The room stood before she sang. She waited, smiling, one hand lifted. When the applause softened, she looked directly at me.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I asked my husband for an ocean, she said. The audience laughed. He brought the whole neighborhood. The laughter became cheering. She let it finish. This is for everybody who came home. Then she sang. Nigga, I have no useful measurement for what her voice did to me that night. I had watched cars leap water. Held a man over a cliff.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Felt blue thunder run through my bones. None of it made the world open the way that first note did when it filled the room we had fought to keep. Rosa joined her. Two voices. Different warmth. Different grief. The same fierce pleasure in being alive enough to make a whole hall listen.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Tank sat forward with both hands clasped so tightly I could see the knuckles change color. That woman, he whispered. I know. Nigga, that woman. I know. On the balcony above us, Celadon held Renee's hand. Nero sat beside Cassius, Livia's letter folded inside his jacket.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Esteban looked at the stage with tears on his face, and Inez rested a hand on his shoulder without interrupting anything he needed to feel. Marcellus turned the Blue Mercy ring once on his finger. Then he stopped touching it and simply listened. When the final note ended, the room stayed quiet for one impossibly long breath. Then everybody stood. I stood first.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Or maybe Tank did. Nigga, we can argue about it when the applause stops. It didn't stop for a long time. Afterward, Cassius found Inez in the courtyard behind the theater. I was there with Shawna, stealing five minutes before the party found us again. We saw him come through the doors carrying no microphone, no huge arrangement, no borrowed confidence from the crowd.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Just a ring. He stopped in front of her. I want to finish the sentence. She looked at his hand. Then at his face. Nigga, finally. He laughed, nervous and happy, and knelt. She said yes before he finished asking. Esteban, watching from the doorway, put one hand over his mouth.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nero slapped him on the back hard enough to make him cough, then hugged him when the coughing turned into laughter. Tank came out at exactly the wrong moment. He saw the ring. Looked at Rosa. Rosa looked back. Nigga, he whispered to me, the whole island putting pressure on me. I put an arm around his shoulders. Drive your own race. He nodded solemnly.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then Rosa kissed his cheek, and the nigga forgot what pressure was. That night Shawna and I went upstairs to the blue room. The harbor lights shone through the curtains. Music drifted from the square. Somewhere below, somebody was still chanting my name with the determination of a man whose friends had tried and failed to get him into a taxi.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna took off her earrings and laid them beside Dante's watch. Then she turned to me. How do you feel, king? I looked at her. At the room she had chosen before she ever stepped inside it. At the sea beyond the window. Nigga, I said, like I brought you to the right place. She came into my arms. You did. We closed the curtains.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The island could keep celebrating without us for a while.
